claims.statement: If A is real symmetric with s_3(A)>=1 and a nonzero original-coordinate scalar pivot a=A_ii is Schur-completed, then the exact Schur complement S satisfies s_2(S)>=1 and e_2(SS^T)>=1.

Every such S has at least one original-coordinate branch: a disjoint cross block B with e_2(BB^T)>=1/48; a one-shared-coordinate determinant bank of squared mass >=1/81; or a principal-pair squared determinant bank >=1/3.

In the disjoint branch, if one selected side has range leverage at most 1/2, the fleet03/B03 determinant-bank half-Riesz theorem and scalar-pivot transducer give ||p_Q||_infinity < 12.450 |A_ii|^{-1/2}; if |A_ii|>=1/4 the bound is <24.900.
For distinct i,j,k, det S[{k,i},{k,j}]=S_kk S^(k)_ij when S_kk!=0, while for S_kk=0 it equals -S_ki S_kj.

A principal-pair squared determinant bank >=1/3 does not force one physical pair determinant bounded below. S_m=direct_sum_{r=1}^m J_m/m has s_2=1, bank mass (m-1)/(2m)>=1/3, but every pair determinant is 0 or 1/m^2. The embedded target family A_m=[1] direct_sum S_m is nevertheless uniformly paid by disjoint block aggregation.

first_unpaid.statement: Find a universal C_H such that for every symmetric S with s_2(S)>=1, independent cap-one product Z, affine ell and constant c, sup_t E|Z^T S Z+ell^T Z+c-t|^{-1/2}<=C_H. After this run the diffuse disjoint-bank subbranch is paid; the exact remaining aggregate debts are high-leverage S0, curved S1, and collective S2.
